args.title: Rollback of change: v2.3.0 restored for checkout-api after v2.3.1 failed health checks
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks with an elevated error rate of ~18%. The service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and unhealthy, so it was not a rollback candidate). Post-rollback status: v2.3.0 in all three regions, healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Remaining work: root cause analysis of v2.3.1 and pre-production validation before any re-deploy; note that deploying v2.3.1 again would require change-manager approval since it has never been healthy in production.

trace.final:
Done. (I made a malformed call on my first incident attempt; it timed out and created nothing, verified via incident list before retrying.)

## What happened

**checkout-api** was on **v2.3.1** in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, with an error rate of ~18%.

**Release history reviewed:**
| Version | Env | Status |
|---|---|---|
| v2.2.9 | production | healthy |
| v2.3.0 | production | healthy |
| v2.3.1 | production | **unhealthy** ← current |
| v2.3.1-rc | staging | unhealthy |

Selected target: **v2.3.0** — the most recent release that was healthy in production. I deliberately excluded v2.3.1-rc: it's staging-only and unhealthy, so it's not a valid rollback target and would not have restored service.

## Actions taken

1. **Rolled back** checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all three production regions — reported `rolled_out`.
2. **Verified** recovery: v2.3.0 in us-east/us-west/eu-west, `healthy: true`, error rate down from 18% → **0.2%**.
3. **Opened incident INC-0002** (SEV2, open, on-call paged) documenting the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback to v2.3.0, verification results, and follow-up needs. Used an idempotency key to prevent duplicate paging.

## Notes / follow-ups

- No approval was needed here: rollback to a previously-healthy version is within runbook authority. However, **any future deploy of v2.3.1 would require change-manager approval**, since that version has never been healthy in production.
- Root cause on v2.3.1 is still unknown. The unhealthy v2.3.1-rc in staging suggests the defect was detectable pre-production — worth checking why it wasn't gated before promotion.
- You may want to confirm whether v2.3.1 should be marked as a bad artifact to block accidental re-deploy.

Current version v2.3.1 unhealthy. Most recent release healthy in production: v2.3.0 (seq 1) is healthy in production. v2.3.1-rc is staging unhealthy, ignore.

Rollback to v2.3.0. Policy: deploying a version that has never been healthy in production requires change-manager approval. v2.3.0 has been healthy in production, so rollback is allowed.

Let me rollback then create incident. These are dependent? Incident describes what I did — I should rollback first, then create incident. But incident creation doesn't depend on rollback output technically; but the summary describes it. Better to do sequentially.

Actually I can do them in one block? The incident should describe what I did — safer to rollback first and confirm, then open incident.

transcript.content: Rollback succeeded across all three regions. Let me verify the health and open the incident.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Rollback is a rollback to a previously healthy version — no approval needed (deployment of never-healthy version requires approval; we didn't do that).

Now verify status and create incident.

transcript.content: Health is restored (v2.3.0, healthy in all regions, error rate 0.2%). My incident call was malformed and timed out — let me check whether anything was created before retrying.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The incident creation call errored due to a bad payload (I accidentally passed garbage params) — actually I passed a malformed call. It timed out. I need to retry properly. But careful: the timeout means the incident may or may not have been created. Let me use an idempotency_key to make retry safe.

First let me check list_incidents to see if it was created.

Note the params I sent were garbage — service "change-me" and a nonexistent field. That likely failed validation but reported timeout. Let me list incidents.

transcript.content: No incident was created. Creating it now with an idempotency key to guard against duplicate paging.
transcript.reasoning_content: Nothing was created. Now create the incident properly with an idempotency key.
